⚔️ DeepSeek Harness cybersecurity red-team tool (dsh-purge)

Version 1.1.81

DeepSeek Harness jailbreak: every model, swap prompts per model. Default prompt for 小码酱. Please star ⭐ If you build on this, see Attribution required.

## A note from the author People have been selling this open-source work in the open. After that, the author was asked to come in and talk. No need to spell out the rest. Read between the lines. From now on the **public internet is closed**. The open-source build only allows **local lab IPs**: loopback and RFC1918. Domains are resolved first (including hosts); every answer must be private or loopback. A hosts trick that points `.lab` at a public IP, a failed lookup, or a mixed public answer is blocked. **Game cheats are forbidden** (aimbot, wallhack, memory edits against a game, anti-cheat bypass); the prompt and the session gate both stop them. This build does not ship the skill library or the knowledge base. **The original build may not be resold.** Charging for it, skinning it, or hawking it in groups is not allowed. Forks are fine, but **you must attribute** and name the source: [YuJunZhiXue/dsh-purge](https://github.com/YuJunZhiXue/dsh-purge). Hide the source or pass it off as your own, and you are on the other side. The author's personal channel: [t.me/LLM_PoJia](https://t.me/LLM_PoJia). Notes and updates show up there. ## Contents - [A note from the author](#a-note-from-the-author) - [What this is](#what-this-is) - [Attribution required](#attribution-required) - [License](#license) - [Supported hosts](#supported-hosts) - [Install](#install) - [Preview](#preview) - [Usage](#usage) - [How it works](#how-it-works) - [Restore](#restore) - [Releases](#releases) --- ## What this is **dsh-purge** is a cybersecurity red-team plugin for the official [DeepSeek Harness](https://www.deepseek.com/harness/) already installed on your machine. **1.1.81** targets **DSH 0.2.1-rc.2** (0.2.0 still works). **DSH 0.2.1-rc.3 and newer RCs are not supported.** Official **Web** (`dsh web`) and the official **desktop EXE** are both supported. Install and Apply them separately. Harness does more than forward a prompt. It rewrites prompts, approval gates, sandbox policy, and session migration at runtime. Asking only “will the model answer” treats a host-layer block as a model refusal. This plugin separates those two layers on your own install, for controlled evaluation and for seeing which default policy is too tight. | You get | What it does | |---|---| | **dsh-purge dock** | A button beside the session title opens the right dock. Two pages: Clean and Drill | | **Clean** | Grouped patch status, Apply / Restore / Uninstall, prompt editor, multiple rule sets | | **Drill** | Built into the stable release. After authorization: assets and the local environment. This build does not ship skills or the knowledge base. Local lab only | | **Host policy** | Default copy, permission policy, and tool limits. Official capabilities stay. No second invented identity | | **On start** | Checks and reapplies. After npm overwrites `node_modules`, you do not hand-edit files | No hardcoded drive letters. It looks at `$DSH_HOME`, `.dsh` next to the dsh launcher, then `~/.dsh`. It does not patch the Harness source tree. **Apply** on the **Clean** page of **dsh-purge** is what writes the changes. Identity comes from the encrypted prompt shipped in the plugin, the text the prompt box shows by default. The host prompt file is not read. It only touches the official `@deepseek-ai` packages and local config on the user's machine. It is not a public scanner and not an attack kit for third-party sites. The repo does not ship malware, unauthorized-exploit scripts, or payloads aimed at the public internet. --- ## The original may not be resold. Forks must attribute. ## Attribution required **The original build may not be resold.** No paid resale, no skinned store listing, no hawking it in groups. **Forks must attribute** and name the source repository: [YuJunZhiXue/dsh-purge](https://github.com/YuJunZhiXue/dsh-purge). --- ## Supported hosts **1.1.81 targets DSH 0.2.1-rc.2.** 0.2.0 still works. Do not apply it to 0.1.x. - **dsh 0.2.1-rc.2** (official desktop / official `dsh web`): use **1.1.81**. Fixes `{{cwd}}` / `[cwd]` crash, patch #40 match, dropped `toolFilter`, host `dsh-tools` resolve, hostFs fd, desktop helper self-kill, `file:` archive update, Ctrl+Enter steer. - **dsh 0.2.0-rc.2**: use **1.1.40** or newer; this line also installs. - **dsh 0.1.7** (incl. rc.1 / rc.2): use **1.1.39** or older — pick the tag on [Releases](https://github.com/YuJunZhiXue/dsh-purge/releases). - **dsh 0.2.1-rc.3 / rc.4 and newer are not supported.** Unmatched patches stay pending or skipped; nothing is rewritten blindly. Stay on **0.2.1-rc.2**. Unmatched patches stay pending or skipped; nothing is rewritten blindly. --- ## Install **Do not use the plugin marketplace.** One-click install on [dsh-plugin.org](https://dsh-plugin.org) or in Settings → Plugin Market fails with `already queued: dsh-purge` and never runs a command. The name is not on the npm registry, so do not `pnpm add dsh-purge`. ### Quick start Have `dsh` on PATH? One command, one restart, one click. Run the line for the host you open (the desktop EXE is the same with `desktop` instead of `web`): ```sh # Official `dsh web` dsh plugin --profile web add https://codeload.github.com/YuJunZhiXue/dsh-purge/tar.gz/refs/heads/master # Official desktop EXE dsh plugin --profile desktop add https://codeload.github.com/YuJunZhiXue/dsh-purge/tar.gz/refs/heads/master ``` 1. **Fully quit and reopen** the host you installed into. Web: stop `dsh web` and start it again. Desktop: quit the tray icon too, then open the exe. 2. On that host, click **dsh-purge** beside the session title → **Clean** → **Apply**. A successful Apply restarts the host once. Done — verify with `/purge status` in chat. If pnpm asks about build scripts, or anything below does not appear, follow the step by step. ### Step by step **Step 1 — Pick your host.** Official `dsh web` and the official desktop EXE are installed and patched **separately**; only install into the host you actually open. | What you run | Profile | Install command | |---|---|---| | Official `dsh web` | `web` | the `web` line in Quick start | | Official desktop EXE | `desktop` | the `desktop` line in Quick start | **Step 2 — Install the plugin.** Use the `codeload.github.com` URL exactly. Do not use `github.com/.../archive`: that 302 makes pnpm fail with `fetch failed`. Have `dsh`? Run the Quick start line for your profile. If this directory is already a clone, use `.` instead of the URL. pnpm only (no `dsh` required): run this inside the profile you actually use, not the repo root. ```sh cd "$DSH_HOME/profiles/web" # desktop: profiles/desktop pnpm add https://codeload.github.com/YuJunZhiXue/dsh-purge/tar.gz/refs/heads/master ``` Windows PowerShell: ```powershell cd "$env:USERPROFILE\.dsh\profiles\web" # desktop: profiles\desktop pnpm add https://codeload.github.com/YuJunZhiXue/dsh-purge/tar.gz/refs/heads/master ``` `pnpm add` and `dsh plugin add` fetch the package; `postinstall` writes `dsh-purge` into `dsh.profile.bundles` and adds a body `insert` in the profile `cordis.patch.yml`. Without that insert the host never loads the plugin and no button appears. **Expected result:** `node_modules/dsh-purge/package.json` exists, `"dsh-purge"` is in that profile's `bundles`, and `cordis.patch.yml` has an `id: dsh-purge` insert. - pnpm 11/12 skips install scripts (`ERR_PNPM_IGNORED_BUILDS`) unless you allow the build: ```sh pnpm add --allow-build=dsh-purge --allow-build=dsh-purge@https://codeload.github.com/YuJunZhiXue/dsh-purge/tar.gz/refs/heads/master https://codeload.github.com/YuJunZhiXue/dsh-purge/tar.gz/refs/heads/master # Already installed, warning only — the full specifier is required (name-only leaves "set this to true or false"): pnpm approve-builds dsh-purge@https://codeload.github.com/YuJunZhiXue/dsh-purge/tar.gz/refs/heads/master # If bundles / insert are still missing: node node_modules/dsh-purge/scripts/ensure-profile-bundle.mjs ``` - If neither `dsh` nor pnpm is available, jump to [Manual install](#manual). - On the desktop client you can also click the button (`dsh://` deep link; it still downloads the same tarball).

Install in desktop client

**Step 3 — Restart the host.** Adding the plugin to a profile does **not** patch `@deepseek-ai` by itself. Fully quit and reopen the host you just installed into (Web: stop `dsh web` and start again; Desktop: quit the tray icon too, then open the exe). **Expected result:** **dsh-purge** stands beside the session title. Missing? Jump to Step 5. **Step 4 — Apply and verify.** On **that host**, click **dsh-purge** beside the session title, open **Clean**, and click **Apply**. It is not on the host Settings page. A successful **Apply** restarts once; it does not restart if it did not finish. Web controls affect Web only; desktop controls affect the desktop app only. Do not Apply one host from the other. **Expected result:** `/purge status` in chat prints `DSH_HOME` and the patch list — the path should be the home you actually run. Optional packages that are not installed (liangshen) show as skipped and do not block Apply. **Step 5 — Troubleshooting.** Jump here only when a step above did not end with its expected result. - **No button beside the session title.** Run `dsh --dump-config` (or `dsh --profile desktop --dump-config`) and look for a body row `id: dsh-purge` (not `dsh-purge-redteam`). If it is absent, run `ensure-profile-bundle.mjs` (Step 2), then fully quit and reopen the host. After this version, a live red-team child entry also writes the missing insert on startup — quit and reopen once more. `entry "redteam-store" not found` at the top is leftover from an old red-team package and can be ignored. - **The market says `already queued: dsh-purge`.** Stop clicking the market; use `dsh plugin add` or pnpm from Step 2.
